newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Vranitzky steps up talks on Albania elections.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky steps up talks on Albania elections.

text.p: International mediator Franz Vranitzky held fresh talks with Albanian President Sali Berisha and political leaders on Thursday to try to resolve differences jeopardising elections planned for June.

Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), diplomatically cancelled a visit to the rebel-held southern Albanian town of Vlore after tough talks with Berisha on Wednesday.
The president told him the elections could not go ahead if the rebels held onto the south.
Vranitzky, looking preoccupied, made no comment to reporters after his hour-long talks with Berisha and immediately began another round of meetings with leading political figures.
He told Berisha on Wednesday that he thought the elections were "in some way imperilled" because of differences between political parties on how to deal with the rebels.
Vranitzky had also urged the government and rebels to hold "at least a minimum of dialogue" to unblock the situation. Berisha refused: "We are not negotiating with them. No."
Reporters were allowed into the talks on Wednesday but not on Thursday. Vranitzky was due to hold a news conference later.
There were few initial signs of progress on Thursday after Vranitzky met Tritan Shehu, chairman of the Democratic Party.
"Legal power must be restored everywhere and some committees which hamper (progress towards the elections) must be eliminated," Shehu told Reuters after the talks.

Albania slid towards anarchy last month in a widespread insurrection sparked by the collapse of dubious pyramid investment schemes that swallowed the life savings of thousands. Nearly 300 people have died in the violence.
Rebels seized control of the south, home of most of the schemes, and have vowed not to give up until Berisha quits.
Medin Xhelili, the head of a regional council in Vlore, said thousands of people had been planning to greet Vranitzky in the port town which touched off the chaos.
"Berisha is plotting against the government and its spirit of reconciliation," he told Reuters.

Berisha blasted the rebel committees as the creation of the Socialist Party, which was the main opposition to Berisha's rightist Democratic Party until the formation of an emergency all-party government last month.
Fatos Nano, a leading Socialist Party figure and former prime minister who was freed from jail last month, praised Vranitzky for his contacts with both sides.

Vranitzky, who met rebel leaders during a trip last month, ran into fierce criticism on Wednesday from pro-Berisha newspapers who said his contacts with the rebels could undermine his neutrality and ruin a return to peace and order.

"He (Vranitzky) is very committed today to continuing the intermediation role with the parties to neutralise the factors that have made the situation stagnate," Nano told reporters before a meeting with Vranitzky.
"Probably he thought it was more important today that the 'rebels' in Tirana be close to one another," he said.
Vranitzky, who had been due to fly from Vlore to a northern town, Shkoder, where fresh violence has flared, was scheduled to meet Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino later.
